questions.question: If the selling price of a bed is 2-times of initial, then the profit is 10-times of initial. Find the initial profit percentage (in %).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling price of bed = 2 × Initial selling price.

Profit = 10 × Initial profit.

**Formula Used:**

Profit Percentage = (Profit / Cost Price) × 100

Let Initial Cost Price = C, Initial Profit = P, and Initial Selling Price = S.

Relation between Selling Price, Profit, and Cost Price: S = C + P

Calculation:

New Selling Price = 2 × S

New Profit = 10 × P

⇒ S = C + P

⇒ 2 × S = C + 10 × P

Substitute S = C + P in 2 × S:

⇒ 2 × (C + P) = C + 10 × P

⇒ 2C + 2P = C + 10P

⇒ 2C - C = 10P - 2P

⇒ C = 8P

Initial Profit Percentage = (P / C) × 100

⇒ Initial Profit Percentage = (P / 8P) × 100

⇒ Initial Profit Percentage = (1 / 8) × 100

⇒ Initial Profit Percentage = 12.5%

**The initial profit percentage is 12.5%.**

questions.question: In a bag containing red, green, and pink tokens, the ratio of red to green tokens was 7 : 20, while the ratio of pink to red tokens was 15 : 12. What was the ratio of green to pink tokens?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of red to green tokens = 7:20

Ratio of pink to red tokens = 15:12

**Formula Used:**

To find the ratio of green to pink tokens, we align the ratios using the common term "red".

**Calculation:**

Ratio of red to green tokens = 7:20

Ratio of pink to red tokens = 15:12

First, express the ratios in terms of a common "red" count:

Let red tokens = 84 (LCM of 7 and 12)

Green tokens = (20 × 84) / 7 = 240

Pink tokens = (15 × 84) / 12 = 105

Now, find the ratio of green to pink tokens:

Green : Pink = 240 : 105

Simplify the ratio:

⇒ Green : Pink = (240 / 15) : (105 / 15)

⇒ Green : Pink = 16 : 7

**The ratio of green to pink tokens is 16:7.**

questions.question: Two pipes, A and B, can fill a tank of 7800 litres in 12 hours and 10 hours, respectively. If they are opened together, how many hours will they take to fill an empty tank of 8800 litres?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Pipe A can fill 7800 litres in 12 hours

Pipe B can fill 7800 litres in 10 hours

Total tank capacity to be filled = 8800 litres

**Formula used:**

Efficiency = Volume ÷ Time

Time taken together = Total volume ÷ (Efficiency of A + Efficiency of B)

**Calculations:**

⇒ A’s efficiency = 7800 ÷ 12 = 650 litres/hour

⇒ B’s efficiency = 7800 ÷ 10 = 780 litres/hour

⇒ Total efficiency = 650 + 780 = 1430 litres/hour

⇒ Time to fill 8800 litres = 8800 ÷ 1430

⇒ Time = (8800)/(1430) = (880)/(143) = (80)/(13)

**∴ Required time = (80)/(13) hours.**

questions.question: A vendor sold 4 chocolates for ₹1, thereby gaining 100%. How many chocolates did he buy for ₹1?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Vendor sold 4 chocolates for ₹1, gaining 100%.

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) of 1 chocolate = ₹(Total SP of 4 chocolates / 4)

Cost Price (CP) of 1 chocolate = SP of 1 chocolate / (1 + Gain %)

Total chocolates bought for ₹1 = ₹1 / CP of 1 chocolate

**Calculation:**

Selling Price (SP) of 4 chocolates = ₹1

SP of 1 chocolate = ₹1 / 4 = ₹0.25

Gain % = 100% ⇒ Gain fraction = 100 / 100 = 1

Cost Price (CP) of 1 chocolate = SP of 1 chocolate / (1 + Gain fraction)

⇒ CP of 1 chocolate = ₹0.25 / (1 + 1)

⇒ CP of 1 chocolate = ₹0.25 / 2

⇒ CP of 1 chocolate = ₹0.125

Total chocolates bought for ₹1 = ₹1 / ₹0.125

⇒ Total chocolates = 1 ÷ 0.125

⇒ Total chocolates = 8

**The vendor bought 8 chocolates for ₹1.**

At the end of the year, the total profit earned is ₹76,700. 31% of the total profit earned is given to charity and the rest is divided among them in the ratio of their investment. What will be the share of Suresh (in ₹)?
questions.solution:

Investment of Alok = ₹56,000

Investment of Gita = ₹52,000

Investment of Suresh = ₹69,000

Charity = 31% of the total profit

Remaining profit = Total profit - Charity

Profit sharing ratio = Ratio of investments (Alok : Gita : Suresh)

**Formula Used:**

Charity = (31 / 100) × Total profit

Remaining profit = Total profit - Charity

Suresh's share = (Suresh's investment / Total investment) × Remaining profit

**Calculation:**

Charity = (31 / 100) × ₹76,700

⇒ Charity = ₹23,777

Remaining profit = ₹76,700 - ₹23,777

⇒ Remaining profit = ₹52,923

Total investment = ₹56,000 + ₹52,000 + ₹69,000

⇒ Total investment = ₹1,77,000

Profit sharing ratio (Alok : Gita : Suresh) = 56,000 : 52,000 : 69,000

⇒ Profit sharing ratio = 56 : 52 : 69

Suresh's share = (69 / (56 + 52 + 69)) × ₹52,923

⇒ Suresh's share = (69 / 177) × ₹52,923

⇒ Suresh's share = ₹20,631

**Suresh's share is ₹20,631.**

questions.question: Robin and Varun together can paint a hall in 6 days. Robin alone can paint it in 42 days. In how many days can Varun alone paint it?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Robin and Varun together can paint in 6 days

Robin alone can paint in 42 days

**Formula used:**

Work = LCM of days taken

Efficiency = Work ÷ Time

Time taken by Varun = Total work ÷ Varun’s efficiency

**Calculations:**

⇒ LCM of 6 and 42 = 42

⇒ Total work = 42 units

⇒ Robin’s 1 day work = 42 ÷ 42 = 1 unit

⇒ Together 1 day work = 42 ÷ 6 = 7 units

⇒ Varun’s 1 day work = 7 - 1 = 6 units

⇒ Time = 42 ÷ 6 = 7 days

**∴ Varun alone can paint the hall in 7 days.**

questions.question: From a taxi stand, two cabs start at a speed of 54 km/hr at an interval of 29 minutes, both cabs travelling in the same direction. A man coming in the opposite direction towards the taxi stand meets the cabs at an interval of 12 minutes. Find the speed (in km/hr) of the man.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of both cabs = 54 km/hr

Time gap between cab departures = 29 minutes

Man meets the cabs at an interval of 12 minutes

**Formula used:**

Distance between cabs = Relative speed (man & cab) × time between meetings

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance between cabs = 54 × (29 ÷ 60) = 54 × 0.4833 = 26.1 km

⇒ Relative speed when man meets cab = Distance ÷ (12 ÷ 60) = 26.1 ÷ 0.2 = 130.5 km/hr

⇒ Man’s speed = Relative speed − Cab speed = 130.5 − 54 = 76.5 km/hr

**∴ The speed of the man is 76.5 km/hr.**

questions.question: Arvind is now 40 years old and Asha is 25 years old. How many years ago from now was Arvind four times as old as Asha?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Arvind's current age = 40 years.

Asha's current age = 25 years.

Calculation:

Let the number of years ago be x .

Arvind's age x years ago = 40 - x .

Asha's age x years ago = 25 - x .

Condition: Arvind's age x years ago = 4 × Asha's age x years ago.

Equation: 40 - x = 4 × (25 - x ).

⇒ 40 - x = 4 × (25 - x

⇒ 40 - x = 100 - 4x

⇒ 40 - 100 = -4x + x

⇒ -60 = -3x

⇒ x = 60 / 3

⇒ x = 20

Arvind was four times as old as Asha 20 years ago.

questions.question: A cook earns ₹8,400 per month. If she spends 60% of it each month, how much will she save (in ₹) by one-fourth of a year?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Monthly income of the cook = ₹8,400

Percentage of income spent = 60%

Time period = One-fourth of a year = 3 months

**Formula Used:**

Monthly savings = Monthly income × (100% - Percentage spent)

Total savings = Monthly savings × Number of months

**Calculation:**

Monthly savings = 8,400 × (100% - 60%)

⇒ Monthly savings = 8,400 × 40%

⇒ Monthly savings = 8,400 × (40 / 100)

⇒ Monthly savings = 8,400 × 0.4

⇒ Monthly savings = ₹3,360

Total savings = Monthly savings × Number of months

⇒ Total savings = 3,360 × 3

⇒ Total savings = ₹10,080

**The cook will save ₹10,080 in one-fourth of a year.**

questions.question: A boat takes 51 minutes to go 10.2 km upstream. The ratio of the speed of the boat in still water to that of the stream is 7 : 6. How much total time (in hours) will the boat take to go 17.7 km upstream and 66.3 km downstream?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Upstream time = 51 minutes = 51 ÷ 60 = 0.85 hours

Upstream distance = 10.2 km

Speed ratio (boat : stream) = 7 : 6

**Formula used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Upstream speed = Boat speed − Stream speed

Downstream speed = Boat speed + Stream speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Upstream speed = 10.2 ÷ 0.85 = 12 km/hr

Let boat speed = 7x, stream speed = 6x ⇒ upstream = 7x − 6x = x

⇒ x = 12 ⇒ boat speed = 7x = 84 km/hr, stream speed = 6x = 72 km/hr

⇒ Downstream speed = 84 + 72 = 156 km/hr

⇒ Time for 17.7 km upstream = 17.7 ÷ 12 = 1.475 hours

⇒ Time for 66.3 km downstream = 66.3 ÷ 156 = 0.425 hours

⇒ Total time = 1.475 + 0.425 = 1.9 hours

**∴ Total time taken = 1.9 hours**

questions.question: An article was bought for ₹1,300. Its price was marked up by 35%. Thereafter it was sold at a discount of 20% on the marked price. What was the percentage profit on the transaction?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹1300

Marked up by 35%

Discount given = 20%

**Formula used:**

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (1 + Markup%)

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (1 − Discount%)

Profit% = ((SP − CP) ÷ CP) × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ MP = 1300 × (1 + 35/100) = 1300 × 1.35 = ₹1755

⇒ SP = 1755 × (1 − 20/100) = 1755 × 0.80 = ₹1404

⇒ Profit = 1404 − 1300 = ₹104

⇒ Profit% = (104 ÷ 1300) × 100 = 8%

**∴ Percentage profit = 8%**
